nodes.name: Dashboard page
nodes.notes:
The page lives inside n8n on purpose. A separate app would mean another container, another DNS record, another deploy and another slice of a memory budget that is already tight -- to draw a page from one query. Here it costs one workflow.

Basic auth, because this is an admin panel on a public hostname and it can launch work. The page shows applicant emails and error payloads, and its buttons re-run automations.

parameters.query:
-- The whole dashboard in one row.
--
-- One query, not one per panel: a page assembled from six reads taken at six
-- slightly different moments can show a creator whose posts are not in the
-- totals yet. A single statement sees one snapshot.
SELECT jsonb_build_object(
  'generated_at', now(),
  'editor_base_url', (SELECT value FROM config WHERE key = 'editor_base_url'),
  -- Only ever rendered into the page's own forms, never shown. See the
  -- action webhook for why it exists.
  'action_token', (SELECT value FROM config WHERE key = 'dashboard_action_token'),

  'funnel', (SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_object_agg(status, n), '{}'::jsonb)
             FROM (SELECT status, count(*)::int AS n FROM submissions GROUP BY status) s),
  -- Distinct applicants, not rows: the bar next to it counts people, and a
  -- replayed-then-failed-again record must not count twice.
  'invalid_total', (SELECT count(DISTINCT COALESCE(payload->>'external_id', md5(payload::text)))::int
                    FROM dead_letters WHERE reason = 'invalid'),

  'creators', (SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(c ORDER BY c.views DESC), '[]'::jsonb) FROM (
      SELECT cr.handle, cr.platform, cr.tracking_code,
             count(p.id)::int AS posts,
             COALESCE(sum(p.views), 0)::bigint AS views,
             COALESCE((SELECT py.amount_cents FROM payouts py
                       WHERE py.creator_id = cr.id
                       ORDER BY py.period_end DESC LIMIT 1), 0)::bigint AS owed_cents
      FROM creators cr
      LEFT JOIN posts p ON p.creator_id = cr.id
      GROUP BY cr.id) c),
  'posts_total', (SELECT count(*)::int FROM posts),
  'views_total', (SELECT COALESCE(sum(views), 0)::bigint FROM posts),

  'runs', (SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(r), '[]'::jsonb) FROM (
      SELECT kind, status, item_count, duration_ms, started_at
      FROM runs ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 12) r),

  'dead_letters_open', (SELECT count(*)::int FROM dead_letters WHERE replayed_at IS NULL),
  'dead_letters', (SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(d), '[]'::jsonb) FROM (
      SELECT id, workflow_name, node, kind, reason, left(error, 240) AS error,
             created_at, execution_url
      FROM dead_letters WHERE replayed_at IS NULL
      ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 10) d),

  'eval', (SELECT to_jsonb(e) FROM (
      SELECT id, ruleset_version, total, correct, accuracy::float AS accuracy,
             macro_f1::float AS macro_f1, started_at
      FROM eval_runs ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1) e),
  'eval_costly', (SELECT to_jsonb(x) FROM eval_costly_errors x
                  WHERE x.eval_run_id = (SELECT max(id) FROM eval_runs)),
  'eval_cases', (SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_agg(ec ORDER BY ec.external_id), '[]'::jsonb) FROM (
      SELECT external_id, expected, actual, correct, note
      FROM eval_cases WHERE eval_run_id = (SELECT max(id) FROM eval_runs)) ec),

  'payout', (SELECT to_jsonb(pp) FROM (
      SELECT period_start, period_end, count(*)::int AS creators,
             sum(amount_cents)::bigint AS total_cents
      FROM payouts GROUP BY period_start, period_end
      ORDER BY period_end DESC LIMIT 1) pp)
) AS state;

nodes.name: Serve the page
nodes.notes: no-store because the page carries applicant data and a live action token, and neither belongs in a proxy or disk cache.

nodes.name: Dashboard action
nodes.notes: Where the buttons post. A plain form post, not a fetch: n8n serves the page with a CSP sandbox that gives it an opaque origin, and a form submission is one of the few things that still works from there.

parameters.query:
SELECT COALESCE(jsonb_object_agg(key, value), '{}'::jsonb) AS config
FROM config;

nodes.name: Token matches?
nodes.notes:
Basic auth is not enough on its own. The browser attaches the saved login to any request for this URL, including a form another website posts here -- so without this check, any page you visit while logged in could launch a replay. The token is rendered only into the dashboard's own forms, which another origin cannot read.

The second condition refuses an empty or short token, so a config row that was never generated cannot be matched by a form that sends nothing.

nodes.name: Back to the dashboard
nodes.notes: Responds before the work starts, not after. A poll takes tens of seconds; the browser goes straight back to the page and watches the numbers move instead of spinning on a button. Nodes after a Respond to Webhook keep running.

nodes.name: Which action?
nodes.notes: Anything that is not one of the three names matches no output and does nothing. The action is a closed list, not a workflow id the browser gets to choose.

nodes.name: Dead letter id
nodes.notes: Only the id crosses into 04. Whether that dead letter exists, is still open and is a replayable kind is decided there, by the same atomic claim the replay webhook uses -- not by trusting what the page said about it.
